value: peak frequency 31.48 kHz (mean +/- SD 0.40; one bat, number of calls not stated)
method: SM4BAT FS recording beside the mist net; analysis in Kaleidoscope 5.4.8
conditions: A single bat captured by mist net in Yarkand County (37°54'24.75"N, 76°47'2.86"E), Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China, July 2023 (specimen SC230705005; sex not stated). Recording condition: free-flying bat, not hand-held; the Methods say a Song Meter SM4BAT FS was 'placed next to the mist net to record bat echolocation calls', analysed in Kaleidoscope v. 5.4.8, and the Results say 'In free-flight outdoor conditions, the pulses are composed of a single harmonic.' The Methods give no recording distance or release procedure and do not say how the recorded calls were attributed to the captured bat (the Abstract says 'we obtained the free-flight echolocation calls of the bat'). The number of calls analysed is not stated; Table 1 ('Echolocation calls features of Barbastella caspica in free-flight conditions.') prints Range and Mean ± SD. The calls are FM; the authors say they resemble Barbastella foraging calls and are 'probably type-I sounds emitted through the mouth' (Abstract), and that 'it is possible that our sound-wave detector failed to capture type-II sounds' (Results and discussion). Peak frequency is stated to be notably low.
